newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Speaker Jose de Venecia announced approval by the House of Representatives of the bill revising the form of excise tax on beer and cigarettes from ad valorem to specific. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Energy Regulatory Board announced that effective Friday prices per litre of premium and unleaded gasoline will be increased by 25 centavos, kerosene by 50 centavos and fuel oil by 3.7 centavos. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Philippine army will launch a house to house search if Christian vigilantes opposed to a peace deal with Moslem rebels defy orders to surrender their weapons, Armed Forces chief General Arturo Enrile said. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- President Ramos has denied an alleged plot by Malacanang to amend the Constitution through a peoples initiative during the May 1997 Barangay elections, saying he will abide by the democratic process and step down in 1998. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- Investment bank Merrill Lynch has projected that the Philippines' current account deficit will reach $2 billion this year and further to $2.4 billion next year. (TODAY)

- The Asian Development Bank has cast doubts on the government's ability to reach its inflation target of 7.5 to 8.5 percent this year. The ADB said in its country economic review the target would be difficult to achieve because the recent deregulation of the oil industry will put pressure on prices of goods and services. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
